tob-10508-75871: The church-teaching volume of Isis Unveiled makes Blavatsky’s boldest claim: that each faith keeps shards of one first wisdom, and that priestcraft spoiled them all. Her sweep through the faiths side by side was unmatched in its reach. The volume sealed her fame — and her ill fame.

tob-4171: Rutherford Platt’s gathering strings the Bible’s lost books and Eden’s forgotten books — the cast-out writ in one volume. His muster bore these barred scriptures to latter-day readers. The tales match the canon in high drama. The book stays the most-bought muster of its kind.

arxiv-2605-08871: Training models across many machines in parallel wastes time waiting for stragglers. Zhirayr Tovmasyan, Artavazd Maranjyan, and Peter Richtárik propose Rennala MVR, a momentum-based variance-reduced method that improves the time complexity of parallel stochastic optimization. The 2026 paper is optimization theory for distributed training.
arxiv-2605-08971: Laser scanners capture buildings as clouds of points; turning them back into CAD models is painstaking. Said Harb, Mehdi Maboudi, and Markus Gerke propose an extrusion segmentation strategy — recognizing parts formed by extruding a profile — to improve the reconstruction. arxiv-2605-09471: Transfer learning borrows from multiple sources, but adaptation is not free — there is a statistical price. Abhinav Chakraborty and Subha Maity quantify the cost of adaptation in multi-source transfer learning. The 2026 paper is learning theory with a price tag.
arxiv-2605-09771: Health outcomes hinge on social determinants — housing, income, environment — as much as on biology itself. This 2026 paper marries a generative model of healthcare events with a digital twin of those social determinants. It is computational epidemiology with a social conscience.
arxiv-2605-09871: The purely singular splitting conjecture — about how certain algebraic structures split apart — finally gets its long-awaited proof. Ka Hin Leung and Tao Zhang deliver it. The 2026 paper is algebra: conjectured for years, then conquered. A clean, complete, satisfying resolution.
plos-pone-0003371: A caution flag for pregnant smokers emerged from this 2008 animal study. Rat pups exposed to nicotine before and after birth suffered progressive damage to the energy-making mitochondria in their pancreases, harming the insulin-producing beta cells. The findings question the assumption that nicotine replacement therapy is fully safe during pregnancy.
plos-pone-0003471: Public-health researchers audited HIV testing in Chennai, India, in this 2008 study. Tracking private labs from 2001 to 2006, they measured whether the growth in voluntary counseling and testing services kept pace with the epidemic's needs. The five-year picture shows who actually used the services and where the diagnostic effort fell short.
plos-pone-0003571: Malaria researchers tracked how humans learn to fight the parasite in this 2008 study. Antibodies that inhibit blood-stage Plasmodium falciparum growth are acquired through exposure, and the team charted how that protective arsenal builds. Understanding the acquisition timeline guides vaccines aiming to shortcut years of natural infection.
plos-pone-0003671: In 2008, Kulkarni, Marconi, and Agan weighed gene copies in the AIDS epidemic. How many copies people carry of the CCL3L1 gene, which feeds into the CCR5 doorway HIV uses, tracked with how fast HIV-1 spread and how well vaccines worked. The gene-dose effect ties a simple copy count to epidemic-scale outcomes.
plos-pone-0003771: Skogsberg, Dicker, and Rydén found the liver talking back to fat in this 2008 paper. The ApoB100-carrying LDL particle acted as a metabolic signal from liver to peripheral fat, putting the brakes on fat breakdown. The reverse message completes a two-way conversation between liver and adipose tissue.
plos-pone-0003871: A 2008 neuroscience study tracked a motor protein at the nerve-muscle junction. Myosin Va was found shaping the plasticity of the vertebrate neuromuscular junction in living animals. The work shows this transport motor tuning the connection that moves muscles.
plos-pone-0003971: In 2008, Watson, MacLean, and Yuste found the cortex tuning out the thalamus at times. During UP states, the active phase of cortical neurons, incoming thalamic signals had less effect. The protective gating lets ongoing cortical activity continue without interruption from outside inputs. The result shows the brain deciding when to listen to the senses and when not.
plos-pone-0004071: In 2008, vanEngelsdorp, Hayes, and Underwood counted America's missing honey bees nationwide. Their survey tracked honey bee colony losses from fall 2007 to spring 2008. Colony Collapse Disorder left hives empty of all workers. The grim numbers set a baseline for the pollinator crisis.
plos-pone-0004171: In 2009, Chang, Lin, and Wu gave cancer drugs a far better address. A new peptide boosted liposomal anti-cancer drugs in mouse lung tumor models. The peptide guided drug bubbles straight to tumors. The neat targeting trick cut the needed dose.
plos-pone-0004271: In 2009, Wodarz and Komarova built math models for cancer-killing viruses. Their models predicted how oncolytic viruses spread through solid tumors fast. The neat equations set the stage for lab validation. The models guide dosing of viral cancer therapy trials ahead.
plos-pone-0338171: Liver surgery saves lives but carries real risks in the days that follow. This study asks whether procalcitonin, a protein that rises in the blood during infection, can serve as an early warning after liver resection. Finding that high levels flag patients heading for complications gives surgeons a simple blood test to spot danger sooner.
plos-pone-0356871: Some breast cancer patients’ tumors vanish entirely under pre-surgery chemo — and doctors want to predict who. This paper built and validated a nomogram, a visual scoring tool, predicting pathologic complete response in luminal-type breast cancer using MammaPrint gene data. The chart helps oncologists personalize treatment plans.
plos-pone-0357971: Heart failure rewires the heart’s genes, and a chemical tag called lactylation may drive it. Combining single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning, this paper identified HMGN2 as a hub gene tied to lactylation in failing hearts. The finding names a new molecular suspect — and a possible drug target — in heart failure.
plos-pone-0356371: Partnerships fail when partners want different things. This paper measured agreement in participant beliefs about the ‘core’ reasons partnerships succeed. The agreement scores reveal whether collaborators are actually on the same page — a practical diagnostic for alliances before they crack under pressure.
plos-pone-0349471: A new plant disease has arrived: the first occurrence of Corynespora cassiicola infecting chia in Bangladesh. This paper documented the outbreak and tested the pathogen’s sensitivity to selected fungicides. The early report gives farmers a fighting chance to act before the fungus spreads to neighboring fields.
plos-pone-0358271: Forecasting PM2.5 air pollution saves lives — but only if the forecast is right. This paper built a deep-learning prediction method integrating improved MSTL decomposition with the FATA optimization algorithm. The hybrid model sharpens smog forecasts for cities choking on fine particles, buying time for protective action.
plos-pone-0357371: Pomegranate peels — usually thrown away — are chemical treasure chests. This paper profiled three Indonesian pomegranate peel varieties for phytochemistry and bioactivity: antioxidant, antibacterial, and more. The results argue persuasively for turning agricultural waste into wellness products.
plos-pone-0346471: Fusing infrared and visible images gives the best of both worlds — heat signatures plus fine detail. DHAFGan is a dense hybrid attention fusion generative adversarial network for infrared-visible image fusion. The network blends the spectra cleanly for surveillance, night driving, and search-and-rescue applications.
plos-pone-0351571: Damaged cultural relics need careful digital restoration. YOLO-WSR combines wavelet features with a structure-guided diffusion model to detect damage and automatically restore cultural heritage artifact images. The AI gives conservators a powerful assistant that respects the original while repairing what time destroyed.
plos-pone-0357571: Encrypting multiple images securely demands chaos — quite literally. ECPD-MIE is an adaptive entropy-controlled chaotic permutation-diffusion scheme for secure multi-image encryption of grayscale and color images. The chaotic mathematics scrambles images beyond recovery for anyone without the key.
plos-pone-0357771: HIV-positive women of reproductive age face elevated risks from high-risk HPV. This study measured the prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes and associated factors among women on antiretroviral therapy. The genotype data give clinicians the evidence to target screening where it matters most.
plos-pone-0337671: Digital health tools for low-resource settings fail when designed without their users. This scoping review protocol will map user-centered design and related participatory approaches in digital health innovations for such settings. The planned review centers the underserved people these tools are meant to serve.
plos-pone-0357671: Two immune-calming drugs — anakinra and tocilizumab — were thrown at severe COVID-19. This single-center sequential cohort study compared their initiation against in-hospital mortality. The head-to-head comparison informs which drug to reach for when the immune system turns on the patient.
plos-pone-0357271: Doping advanced ceramics with samarium and nickel tunes their optical and electrical behavior. This paper studied the effects of Sm and Ni co-doping on lead magnesate niobate titanate ceramics. The doping recipe optimizes performance for the demanding applications these materials serve.
plos-pone-0350771: Activated charcoal filtration during hepatic chemosaturation — a liver cancer procedure — profoundly alters systemic noradrenaline. This prospective cohort study measured those concentration changes. The finding matters for managing patients through a procedure that already stresses the body intensely.
plos-pone-0357171: COVID-19 vaccination uptake among Nigerian women of reproductive age split sharply along socioeconomic lines. This paper decomposed those inequalities using population-based data. The decomposition shows policymakers exactly where equity efforts must aim.
plos-pone-0356771: Counting livestock on crowded farms — where animals pile on top of each other — defeats ordinary detectors. DOLD-Net tackles dense occluded livestock detection via global-local feature collaboration. The network sees the herd both as a whole and animal by animal, giving farmers reliable automated headcounts even in the crush.
plos-pone-0354671: Detecting HPV DNA in blood could transform cervical disease monitoring. This paper applied Cobas 6800 HPV testing plus qPCR with three genomically-optimized primer sets to find HPV DNA in the blood of patients with HPV-positive dysplasia and cancer. The blood-based approach inches toward a liquid biopsy for cervical disease.
plos-pone-0340571: Food handlers silently carrying drug-resistant gut bacteria threaten everyone they serve. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the burden of fecal colonization with ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae among food handlers in Africa. The pooled prevalence is a wake-up call for food safety regulation.
plos-pone-0351471: Cocklebur — Xanthium strumarium — is spreading as the climate shifts, and its root-zone microbes may help it invade. This Chinese study integrated species distribution models with rhizosphere microbiome analysis to project climate change impacts on the weed’s range. The combined approach reveals where this aggressive plant will march next.
plos-pone-0356171: Coaches who genuinely involve young athletes produce better outcomes — but the evidence was scattered. This scoping review mapped youth participation coach learning. The synthesis gives sports organizations a coherent picture of how to train coaches who empower rather than merely instruct.
plos-pone-0354371: Running parents pushing strollers wonder whether the extra load courts injury. This paper examined injury risk and running habits in parents — asking whether stroller use makes a difference. The findings give running moms and dads evidence-based guidance on training safely with a passenger aboard.
plos-pone-0354471: Sharing human genomic data across borders — especially involving low- and middle-income countries — raises thorny questions. This systematic review examined data sharing practices in collaborative genomic research in these settings. The findings reveal who benefits from shared genomes — and who merely provides them.
plos-pone-0354971: Sports officials — referees and umpires — endure psychological pressures few acknowledge. This paper evaluated the psychosocial effects of the Northern Territory Institute of Sport’s High Performance Officiating Program. The findings illuminate what elite officiating does to wellbeing — and how programs can protect it.
plos-pone-0353971: Disease clusters hide in geographic data — and finding them takes the right statistics. This paper integrated disease mapping with flexible scan statistics to identify and visualize spatial clusters. The combined approach gives epidemiologists sharper tools for spotting outbreaks’ geographic fingerprints.
europmc-pmc2799471: Bisphenol A, a man-made compound in many plastics, can reach babies before birth through their mothers. This 2009 study asks what that means for how young children act. europmc-pmc2854771: Silver particles kill germs, but do they wound skin? This 2010 study tests silver nanoparticle harm on live skin and lab-grown skin cells. The team charts where the particles lodge and bite. Their read steered safe use in creams and dressings.
europmc-pmc2858671: Brains pack dense wiring into tight skulls, a feat chip makers envy. The work linked neuroscience to better computer hardware.
europmc-pmc2864571: RNA can fold into working shapes, and many remain undiscovered. This 2010 paper hunts them across bacteria, archaea, and their metagenomes, netting 104 candidate structured RNAs. europmc-pmc2866471: A shellfish-derived compound can guard crops, this 2010 review reports. The authors survey chitosan in plant protection, covering how it fights pests and disease. Their overview backs a natural alternative to harsh chemicals. The review helped move chitosan from lab curiosity to field tool.
europmc-pmc2967471: Gentle electric waves can tune the brain's own rhythm. This 2010 study shows scalp-applied alternating current boosts each person's alpha waves in EEG. The authors show the tuning works. Their work opened a path to noninvasive brain care. Future treatments may ride these waves.
europmc-pmc3039971: Nature's soaps can clean up pollution. This 2011 review covers germ-made soaps for green cleanup jobs. The authors survey recent wins. Their overview guides eco-remediation. europmc-pmc3043071: Gender surgery outcomes got long-term data. This 2011 Swedish study follows people for years after gender-affirming surgery. The authors' long follow-up informs care. europmc-pmc3061871: Breast cancer outlooks went online. This 2011 paper brings GOBO, a web tool that predicts breast cancer outcomes from gene data. The authors' site served doctors and patients. Their tool spread widely. Thousands queried it for second opinions. The tool is free for all users.
europmc-pmc6658471: Genetic risk scores work best for Europeans - because most studies enrolled Europeans. The paper is a wake-up call: risk prediction must diversify or it will serve only some.
europmc-pmc6751071: One in ten babies arrives early - and the vaginal microbiome may help explain why. europmc-pmc6777271: Cancer's global toll is staggering - and uneven. This Global Burden of Disease analysis tallies cancer incidence, deaths, years lost, and years lived with disability across countries. The ledger shows where the burden falls hardest and where progress lags.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-71: GAO's 2007 report revisits the poisoned town of Libby, Montana — and the far-flung sites that took its tainted ore. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1071: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report finding the Export-Import Bank needed to improve how it assessed the economic impact of its financing. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-671: Moving military families was a logistical tangle in 2007 — GAO's report says the Pentagon needed one coherent plan for its new household-goods system. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-371: The bank insurance funds got an audit in 2007, and GAO's report grades the FDIC funds' financial statements for 2006 and 2005. The findings deliver the formal opinion. openalex-w7206216571: When a boss bullies a subordinate in the military, the chain of command makes it worse. pmc-13520471: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of theracal's efficacy as a pulp capping material in permanent dentition. The dental material's performance was pooled. The review guides endodontics.
pmc-13441271: A 2026 case report of acquired hemophilia A presenting with hematoma, hemarthrosis, and hemotympanum. The bleeding disorder's dramatic face was documented. The case is the lesson.
pmc-13440771: In this 2026 case series and literature review, transarterial embolization of a ruptured distal choroidal artery aneurysm in Moyamoya disease was reported. The delicate embolization was detailed. The series guides intervention.
pmc-13425871: A 2026 paper on co-development of a research-to-policy framework for Indonesia's health policy-making — a multiperspective approach. The framework was codesigned. The co-development is the model.
pmc-13547371: In this 2026 paper, early life sugar rationing was linked to ageing-related diseases, biological ageing, and mortality. The wartime rationing's longevity legacy was measured. The linking is the epidemiologic insight.
pmc-13472571: A 2026 paper with integrated genetic identification and molecular dynamics simulations of a novel LOXL3 mutation associated with Stickler syndrome. The mutation's mechanism was modeled. The integrating is the diagnostic advance.
pmc-13452271: A 2026 mouse study: sea buckthorn polyphenols improved lipid metabolism via gut-liver axis modulation in db/db mice. The berry's metabolic benefit ran through the gut. The improving is the mechanism.
pmc-13643671: A 2026 veterinary paper comparing CT versus MRI for perioperative management of acute thoracolumbar intervertebral disc extrusion in non-ambulatory dogs (the title is truncated). The imaging modalities were head-to-head. The comparison guides veterinary neurology.
pmc-13417471: A 2026 retraction notice for a paper claiming Ganoderma lucidum and Auricularia polytricha mushrooms protected against carbofuran-induced toxicity in rats. The paper was withdrawn. The retraction amends the record.
pmc-13418871: A 2026 resting-state fMRI study of frequency-dependent alterations of degree centrality in poststroke depression patients. The depressed stroke brain's networks were mapped. The alterations are the biomarker.
arxiv-2606-16371: Training neural networks relies on optimizers, and Muon is a newer one that needs a costly "polar factor" computation. CacheMuon speeds it up with temporal preconditioning — reusing information across steps to approximate that factor cheaply. The paper presents the optimizer tweak for researchers training large models who want Muon's benefits without its cost.
arxiv-2606-16571: A quasi-kernel is a small set of vertices in a directed graph from which everything else is reachable in at most two steps. This graph-theory paper studies quasi-kernels in hereditary classes — families closed under taking subgraphs — with applications to "break digraphs." It targets specialists in structural graph theory.
arxiv-2606-16671: Training models means solving optimization problems, and curvature (the Hessian) changes along the way. This paper — part one of a series — gives a Chebyshev-exact acceleration method that adapts to that changing curvature, via the 'Sine-Jacobi' method. It is for optimization researchers.
arxiv-2606-16871: AI agents need evaluation, but tests don't scale to every task. 'Human-on-the-Bridge' proposes scalable evaluation with humans in the loop at key checkpoints. It is for researchers who need trustworthy agent benchmarks without infinite human labor. People at the helm, scale intact.
